macro.headline: Hawkish Fed, energy & geopolitics in the driver's seat
macro.body: Fed Chair Warsh scrapped forward guidance and the dot plot leans toward hikes, not cuts, so long-duration high-multiple growth (NOW, ADBE, NVDA, IOT) stays rate-sensitive. Energy and the Strait of Hormuz headlines are the live swing factor on inflation.

risk.detail: FY guide cut (Jun 4): Americas comps −5% (5th straight), tariffs gutted margins, China stalled.
FY26 growth cut 10.5→7–8.5%; Watchman/EP/urology soft; mgmt guides flat through Q3.
Beat & raised (Jun 11) yet sold off; AI-moat fear (Claude Design), CFO exit, ARR de-emphasis — the narrative, not the numbers, drives it.
China export-license tightening + Senate scrutiny; the memory/chip complex swings on AI-spending sentiment.
No bad news — strong Q1, IBM AI deal. But it's the biggest weight + a high multiple; in a hawkish-Fed software de-rate it leads the drawdown.
Trump MFN pricing deals (Gilead, Novartis signed) + import tariffs put a pricing-pressure overhang on the whole pharma cluster.
FY EPS guide cut on deal financing + a weak flu season; revenue raised. Defensive — a yellow flag, not a red one.

sectors.driver: A broader market rally as oil prices retreat
sectors.note: Amid a broader market rally as oil prices retreat, bond yields stabilize and U.S. CPI data confirms investor expectations that the Fed will hike rates at its September meeting.

sectors.driver: Sympathy with Snowflake after the company reported better-than-expected …
sectors.note: Amid sympathy with Snowflake after the company reported better-than-expected Q2 financial results, boosting sentiment across the sector. Falling Treasury yields and Fed's Waller's comments that he is inclined to support holding interest rates steady may also be supporting growth stocks by easing concerns about tighter monetary policy and improving risk appetite.

sectors.driver: Stabilizing bond yields and oil price retracement
sectors.note: Amid stabilizing bond yields and oil price retracement. Also, Oracle executives on the Q1 conference call noted a high capex commitment to server infrastructure and continued sector-wide server demand.

sectors.driver: Possible sympathy with Comcast after its CFO said at a conference that Q…
sectors.note: Amid possible sympathy with Comcast after its CFO said at a conference that Q3 broadband subscriber losses are unlikely to improve year-over-year and that fiber connectivity pricing has become "irrational.".

sectors.driver: Optimism regarding the U.S.-Iran dispute and improved transport through …
sectors.note: Amid optimism regarding the U.S.-Iran dispute and improved transport through the Strait of Hormuz. More chemicals and feedstocks exiting the Persian Gulf may hinder pricing power and margins for companies that benefited from recent product shortages.
